evidence.text: Construct and extremize the N=1 F-term potential using the tree-level, large-volume Kähler potential. Determine physical masses through the inverse Kähler metric times the half-Hessian, and evaluate F-terms and the gravitino mass.

evidence.text: Engineer common flux scaling by selecting a subset of superpotential terms, typically n+1 flux parameters for n complex moduli. Equal scaling of these terms predicts vev scaling; explicit extrema supply model evidence.

sources.title: A Flux-Scaling Scenario for High-Scale Moduli Stabilization in String Theory

evidence.text: Use a twisted differential with nilpotency constraints for flux Bianchi identities, flux-induced tadpoles, and gauge invariance of the superpotential under D7-induced axion shifts to derive generalized Freed–Witten constraints.

evidence.text: Use gradient flow, differentiate the approximate velocity, form its determinant with acceleration and eliminate H with potential domination. The local polynomial is an input to this method, not the method itself.

evidence.text: Combine instanton-induced 't Hooft determinant interactions with four-fermion terms obtained by integrating out the Stückelberg vector. Fierz rearrangement exposes Nambu–Jona-Lasinio channels; confinement and condensation motivate a nonlinear-sigma-model EFT.

sources.title: Runaway Relaxion Monodromy

evidence.text: Appendix B uses Chern–Simons couplings, Poincaré duality, and holomorphic-curve arguments to assert that a supersymmetric D7 stack with nonzero relaxion coupling must intersect the NS5 cycle as point sets, even when the corresponding topological intersection number vanishes.

sources.title: Cosmic birefringence from monodromic axion dark energy

evidence.text: Evolve a specified potential from a frozen initial field, select the initial value to reproduce the present abundance, and translate the resulting displacement into a coupling. The principal application fixes the axion to all dark energy.

sources.title: Axion flux monodromy discharges relax the cosmological constant

evidence.text: Integrate out the massive axion at its minimum, then use thin-wall semiclassical Euclidean instantons between locally maximally symmetric backgrounds. O(4)-symmetric geometries are glued with gravitational junction conditions, and transition rates are estimated as Γ∼exp(−Sbounce). Several derivational details are delegated to earlier work.

sources.title: Runaway Relaxion Monodromy

evidence.text: Dimensional reduction of fivebrane DBI and Chern–Simons actions identifies the secular potential, quantized induced D3 charge, and transverse brane KK modes. The probe action is then contrasted with the action including those charges as ten-dimensional sources.

sources.title: Runaway Relaxion Monodromy

evidence.text: Backreaction is expanded perturbatively in N/ND3 around a warped conifold background, using harmonic decomposition of metric and flux perturbations. Open/closed-string duality supplies a complementary interpretation through D3–D7 string threshold corrections to the gauge coupling.

sources.title: Cosmic birefringence from monodromic axion dark energy

evidence.text: Use an integrating factor to isolate a force-driven trajectory and a decaying initial-data transient. Applied to axion dark energy, this explains why recent displacement mainly tracks the local potential slope.

destinations.title: Can wrapped-brane monodromy extend a single closed-string axion through a controlled super-Planckian inflationary trajectory while preserving moduli stabilization, and what observables follow?

Can axion–four-form monodromy support high-scale quadratic inflation over a super-Planckian excursion while controlling ultraviolet corrections, moduli backreaction, winding-induced light states and transitions between branches?

Can replacing five-brane monodromy sources with [p,q] seven-branes yield protected large-field axion inflation with enhanced tensor modes, improved microscopic control, or restored supersymmetry after inflation?

Can axion–four-form monodromy sustain approximately quadratic, large-field inflation in a high-scale string setting, and can nearby UV scales produce observable corrections without destabilizing inflation?

How do multiple axion-monodromy inflatons change the allowed scalar tilt n_s and tensor-to-scalar ratio r relative to the corresponding single-field potential, and how do these predictions depend on distributions of potential coefficients and initial field values?

Which large-field axion potentials arise from flux-induced monodromy when the inflationary energy also participates in moduli stabilization, and how does modulus adjustment change the final monomial exponent and inflationary predictions?

Can type IIB three-form fluxes produce single-field F-term axion monodromy with one parametrically light axion, all other complex-structure fields and the axio-dilaton stabilized, and a suitable trans-Planckian potential?

Can flux tuning produce a sufficiently light F-term axion monodromy inflaton while controlling complex structure backreaction, preserving Kähler moduli stabilization, and leaving a substantial population of acceptable flux vacua?
Can tree-level stabilization with geometric and non-geometric fluxes provide perturbative control and the mass hierarchy needed for high-scale, single-field F-term axion monodromy inflation?

Can a localized D6-brane generate large-field axion monodromy inflation with stabilized heavier moduli, a stable inflationary trajectory, and a computable potential beyond the small-field supergravity regime?
Can a minimal string construction produce an isolated axion-monodromy inflaton from a warped KK mode, and can its geometry remain controlled over a sufficiently large field excursion?

How do converged mirror-quintic periods change flux-vacuum existence, conifold hierarchies and possible inflationary regions, relative to low-order period approximations? Can the axionic directions support single-field monodromy inflation in the studied no-scale setting?

How should membrane-mediated branch tunneling in a rolling axion-monodromy background be estimated when Coleman vacuum-decay assumptions fail, and what conditional constraints follow for inflation and relaxation?

Can a massive compact U(1) gauge-theory description explain why large-field axion monodromy inflation is protected from dangerous ultraviolet corrections, and interpret its inflaton dynamics through defect condensation?

Can generic background fluxes produce stronger flattening of D7-brane axion-monodromy inflation than previously studied flux choices, while supporting a light inflaton, closed-string moduli stabilisation and acceptable cosmological observables?
Can two axionic inflatons coexist with stabilized moduli, separated ultraviolet scales, acceptable perturbations and a large potential gradient in a flux-scaling effective theory?

destination.title: Formulating cosmological entropy bounds
destination.question: Which entropy bound is appropriate to a specified cosmology, and how do geometry, thermodynamic laws, quantum corrections and counting conventions delimit it?
destination.summary: Compares cosmological bound prescriptions without imposing one dimension, cosmological-constant sign or entropy definition.

sources.title: Role of the cosmological constant in the holographic description of the early universe

evidence.text: How should a positive cosmological constant enter holographic bounds for a radiation-dominated universe: as geometric entropy, vacuum energy, or a parameter of an elliptic-curve description?

sources.title: Holographic cosmology and its relevant degrees of freedom

evidence.text: Can a global, time-symmetric modification of the Fischler–Susskind bound become viable and stringent in four-dimensional cosmologies with zero cosmological constant by counting history-compatible states rather than instantaneous entropy?

sources.title: Positive vacuum energy and the N bound

evidence.text: Does every universe with a positive cosmological constant obey an observable-entropy bound S ≤ N = 3π/Λ, including matter-dominated and recollapsing universes that never approach de Sitter space?

sources.title: The Entropy of the microwave background and the acceleration of the universe

evidence.text: If cosmic acceleration comes from a positive cosmological constant, is the microwave-background entropy measurable by a local observer bounded parametrically below the entropy of empty de Sitter space?

sources.title: Positive vacuum energy and the N bound

evidence.text: Derives the D-bound through a generalized-second-law process: the observer moves into an asymptotically empty de Sitter region, losing access to matter while cosmological horizon entropy increases by (A₀−A_c)/4.

sources.title: Role of the cosmological constant in the holographic description of the early universe

evidence.text: Use a Newtonian point-mass model with ri(t) = S(t)ri(t0), cosmological force Fi = (Λ/3)miri and potential Vc = −(Λ/6)Σmiri². Rescaling the energy equation produces a Friedmann-shaped equation.

sources.title: The Entropy of the microwave background and the acceleration of the universe

evidence.text: Use the generalized Birkhoff theorem, continuity of the interface metric, and Israel junction conditions to match the dust interior to the exterior and relate its mass parameter to interior entropy.

sources.title: Holographic cosmology and its relevant degrees of freedom

evidence.text: Compares horizon trajectories and areas in de Sitter space and closed Robertson–Walker cosmologies. The closed-universe discussion uses the horizon coordinate χ(t)=∫₀ᵗdt′/R(t′) and an equation-of-state parameter γ.

sources.title: Positive vacuum energy and the N bound

evidence.text: Imports the covariant entropy bound S ≤ A/4 on orthogonal null light-sheets whose cross-sectional area is everywhere nonincreasing. Sheets terminate at or before caustics; truncation at area A′ permits the strengthened bound S ≤ (A−A′)/4.

sources.title: Positive vacuum energy and the N bound

evidence.text: Classifies spherical diamonds by maxima on their top and bottom cones. Auxiliary asymptotically de Sitter extensions allow the D-bound to constrain normal-side portions; the covariant bound controls remaining light-sheets, with complementary area terms giving S ≤ N.

sources.title: Holography in radiation dominated universe with a positive cosmological constant

evidence.text: Can the holographic relation between closed radiation-universe Friedmann equations and Cardy–Verlinde entropy survive a positive cosmological constant, and can a moving brane in Schwarzschild–de Sitter space realize saturation of the proposed entropy bound?

sources.title: Probable ratio of the vacuum energy in a Schwarzschild-de Sitter space

evidence.text: Can a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) heuristically modify Schwarzschild–de Sitter horizon thermodynamics so as to select a probable vacuum-energy fraction, explain a small effective cosmological constant, and connect entropy bounds?

sources.title: Holography and the generalized second law of thermodynamics in (2+1)-dimensional cosmology

evidence.text: Does the Fischler–Susskind (FS) entropy bound survive negative cosmological constant in (2+1)-dimensional cosmology, and which cosmological entropy bound is compatible with classical or quantum-modified generalized second laws (GSL)?

sources.title: Information-theoretic constraints in quantum gravity and cosmology

evidence.text: Which information-theoretic entropy constraints survive quantum matter effects in semiclassical gravity, and how can entanglement and causality constrain holographic descriptions of de Sitter and closed cosmological spacetimes?

sources.title: Black holes in de Sitter space: Masses, energies and entropy bounds

evidence.text: Can cosmological horizons admit distinct, physically motivated energy and mass definitions, consistent thermodynamics, and entropy bounds based on energy inside a bounded de Sitter region?

sources.title: Holography and cosmology

evidence.text: How should the holographic entropy bound be formulated in cosmology, and what conditional restrictions would it impose on expansion, the equation of state, and spatial curvature?

sources.title: Holographic entropy bounds in the inflationary universe

evidence.text: Which holographic entropy bounds can describe slow-roll inflation, reheating and the subsequent radiation era, modeled respectively using de Sitter space, radiation with positive cosmological constant and radiation alone?
